args: In Access Buddy, on the request an access update flow that members submit, can we please make it very clear that members should not submit this request for an expired fob. Expired fobs will be reactivated as part of the membership renewal form. You do not need to submit an access update. Submitting an extra form is likely to slow to process down.

args:
Ev charging ha brief · MD
EV Charging Monitor — Home Assistant Implementation Brief
Goal
Monitor BYD Shark 6 charging at a share house via a smart plug, attribute each charge session to solar vs grid, and calculate a fair cost split so the car owner can reimburse the household accurately.

Fair-share formula (agreed approach):

Solar portion of car draw = energy the house would otherwise have exported → charged at the feed-in tariff (opportunity cost)
Grid portion = the rest → charged at the consumption tariff
Per interval: solar_to_car = min(car_power, grid_export_excluding_car); grid_to_car = car_power - solar_to_car
Current state (done — do not redo)
Hardware: Athom Smart Plug V3 (ESP32-C3, 16A relay, energy monitoring) between wall GPO and a 10A/1.5mm² extension lead to the BYD portable charger. Charge draw ~2.3 kW (~10 A) sustained.
Firmware: stock Athom ESPHome firmware, updated to latest. An earlier API connection crash loop was resolved by updating both HA and the plug firmware to current versions (API version mismatch). BLE proxy is still enabled; if API instability or boot loops recur, the known fix is adopting the plug in ESPHome Device Builder and rebuilding with esp32_ble_tracker: !remove and bluetooth_proxy: !remove. API encryption enabled; key lives in the ESPHome device YAML.
HA: updated to latest version, network 192.168.68.x. Device name/hostname: athom-smart-plug-v3-4cb818.
Plug is connected via the ESPHome integration. Verify before building on it: entities for switch, power (W), current, voltage, energy (kWh) exist and update.
Solar (needs discovery — ask before implementing)
House solar is a Sungrow inverter viewed via iSolarCloud (WiNet/WiFi dongle).

Preferred: local Modbus TCP to the WiNet dongle, port 502, using the mkaiser Sungrow-SHx-Inverter-Modbus-Home-Assistant HACS package. Needs dongle on the LAN and Modbus enabled.
Fallback: GoSungrow → MQTT (cloud, ~5 min lag; acceptable for billing, poor for automation).
Open question: does the inverter have a Sungrow smart meter (i.e. does HA get grid import/export, not just PV production)? If no meter, solar attribution needs a CT clamp on the grid supply (e.g. Shelly EM) or must degrade to "PV production minus estimated house load" with clearly documented assumptions.
To build
Tariff inputs: known rates — consumption 24 c/kWh (flat); feed-in is tiered: 8 c/kWh for the first 8 kWh exported per day, 2 c/kWh thereafter. Model as input_number helpers so rates stay adjustable. The tiered FIT matters for solar valuation: the correct rate for solar diverted to the car is the marginal feed-in rate at that moment, i.e. track daily total export with a utility_meter; value car-solar at 8 c while daily export (including what the car consumed of it) is under 8 kWh, 2 c after. If that's too fiddly for v1, a documented simplification (e.g. flat 8 c) is acceptable, but flag it on the dashboard.
Energy accounting:
Riemann sum (left, kWh) on plug power → car energy
Template sensor splitting instantaneous car power into solar/grid portions per the formula above (guard for sensor unavailability; treat unknown solar as 100% grid so the household is never undercharged)
Riemann sums on both portions → car_solar_kwh, car_grid_kwh
utility_meter helpers on all three: daily + monthly cycles
Cost sensors: monthly car_cost = car_solar_kwh × feed_in + car_grid_kwh × consumption, exposed in dollars, plus a per-session cost if practical (session = relay on→off or power above ~100 W threshold).
Automation (optional, behind an input_boolean.solar_charge_mode): turn plug on when grid export > 2.3 kW sustained 10 min; off when import > threshold sustained 10 min. Include input_boolean.charge_now manual override that forces the plug on. Avoid rapid cycling (min 10-min dwell).
Dashboard: current charge power, session energy/cost, month-to-date solar vs grid kWh and $ owed, tariff inputs, override toggles. Add plug sensors to the HA Energy dashboard (individual device).
Constraints and cautions
Plug relay must never rapid-cycle under 10 A load; any automation needs dwell times.
Do not
